note: Cause found 2026-11-09 by tracing every request the ADSP makes (a verbose hexagonrpcd build on the phone): the sensors service (hexagonrpcd -s) attaches the ADSP sensor process, whose registry init re-reads the sensor configs and needs to write (temp.json); hexagonrpcd refuses all writes, the firmware asserts (SNS_REG_INIT) and the whole ADSP restarts, taking audio with it. No registry state fixes it (packaged, or the phone own from persist, readable, with the version marker - which hexagonrpcd also never serves: a real gap, patch drafted). Fix in place on the phone: hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd masked. Result: 0 ADSP crashes across three boots and many minutes, the POCO X3 sound card up at about 12 s, playback without crashes. Trade-off: no ADSP sensors, which did not work anyway. Next: propose upstream (do not start sensorspd on surya until registry writes are supported; serve sns_reg_version in hexagonrpcd); see sensors-registry-writes.
title: The ADSP crashes every 13-25 s, restarting audio each time

note: Found 2026-11-10 on Sxmo (sensors service masked, all fixes in): 8 ms after resume from s2idle the ADSP reports a fatal error (EX:kernel:0x0:IST46:0x132:PC=0xf0049be4) and restarts; its audio services are back about 0.25 s later and playback works again. 2 of 3 suspends crashed it. Sxmo suspends whenever the screen is off, so playback is cut at wake-ups. Lead, not yet tested: the kernel may drop the ADSP's power or resource votes during s2idle (upstream once had to keep a remote processor's load state unaltered across suspend). The automatic adsp-stable check counts crashes right after a resume. Narrowed 2026-11-10: 2 crashes in 28 suspends of one boot, both early in it (at 51 s and 839 s), none in the following 26 - not suspend alone, not audio playing or just played, not the sound card (unbound or bound), not I2C access to the amps, not the time awake (a 12-cycle soak, 10 s to 5 min, all clean). Lesson: dmesg is a ring that this kernel's debug prints overwrite within minutes; crash counts now come from the journal.
title: The audio DSP crashes right after resume from suspend

note: With the sensors service off, one boot (2026-11-09) never announced the ADSP audio services, so no sound card until the ADSP was restarted by hand. Not reproduced in two further valid cold boots (audio services about 0.1-0.2 s after the ADSP, card present). Watch for it; if it recurs, check whether the in-kernel pd-mapper was loaded before the ADSP booted.
title: One cold boot came up without audio services

note:
Asked for 2026-11-10: the conveyor as a repo of its own, so anyone can bring support to another phone with the same conveyors, CI, tests, tad page and automatic integration into the grand picture; surya is the first instance, not the mould.

Design. (1) linux-phone-oco/device-template, a GitHub template repository: Use this template makes <vendor>-<codename>-lab. (2) device.toml, one manifest per device - codename, SoC, compatible strings, panel variants, image sources, how to reach the phone - read by every script; no script edited per device. (3) Generic machinery, generalized from surya-lab: the phone library (USB or Wi-Fi, commands on stdin), flashing with built-in fixes, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi from private files), switching shells, device-tree audits, an upstream queue with send commands generated by get_maintainer.pl. (4) Tests as small independent checks, one file each declaring its component and what it needs, so a device runs the checks that apply; results as JSON lines with a versioned schema. (5) Device-independent analysis in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools (Rust): tone (speaker tests microphone) first. (6) Onboarding conveyor: a lab-tools command reads a running phone (compatible, inputs, outputs, sound devices) and fills device.toml - and from the same facts generates the Sxmo device profile. (7) Each device repo publishes its own tad data (support status, test runs, wiki claims) with CI that validates it and renders its page. (8) Integration: a feed in linux-phone-oco/docs discovers device repos by a GitHub topic and pulls their published tables, so a new device appears in the devices table and the support grid (tad draws device x component as a matrix) with no hand edits. (9) Conventions in AGENTS.md: explicit intent for state changes, lists as arguments, secrets outside repos, fingerprints before trusting images. (10) Proof: surya-lab re-based onto the template as its first instance - still 18 of 18 through it. Landscape read 2026-11-10 (see the landscape table): build on what exists - device.toml derives from postmarketOS deviceinfo; tests take the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI tests and use bootrr for driver probes; the lab aims to be a CI-tron-compatible setup and surya a device under test in pmOS's hardware farm; flashing leans on pmbootstrap.
title: A device template: the conveyor any phone's support is built on

note: The microphones go through the WCD9375 codec, which the stock device tree does not wire up (the sound card has only the speaker). Needs the device-tree work on linux-phone-oco/linux PR #1 (aoncc dropped, VA macro clocked from q6afecc; built and audited, not yet booted). Test idea: play a tone on the speaker and record it, so the check needs no ears. Boot test needs the user nearby (a hang needs the power button). Prior art found by the kernel-activity feed (2026-11-10): upstream sm7150-mainline committed "WIP WCD stuff" to the surya device tree (7b00a934ace1, 2026-03-28, Aelin Reidel) and reverted it (6ec3051564fd, 2026-05-17). Read both, and why it was reverted, before booting our WCD9375 device tree. Built 2026-11-10 on the lab machine: a whole test kernel, 7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd (the phone's exact v7.1_rc3 source + upstream's WIP WCD patch + our tas2562 fix; the pin-controller drivers it changes are built in, so modules alone cannot carry it): Image.gz, the Huaxing dtb and 828 modules under ~/Projects/surya-audio/kernel-rc3/{src-wcd,out-wcd}. Test plan, safe: a second systemd-boot entry (pmos-wcd.conf: its own kernel, initramfs and dtb), stock stays the default; a loader.conf with a 10 s menu (Nura ships none, so there is no menu); pick the entry with the volume keys, or try a one-shot boot; a hang falls back to stock on reboot. To check on the phone: whether the menu takes the volume keys, and an initramfs for the -wcd version (mkinitfs builds for the installed kernel). Needs the user nearby. Progress 2026-11-10: the WCD test kernel (upstream WIP + our tas2562 fixes) boots; wcd937x probes and both SoundWire devices bind; then the controller at 62ed0000 reports a bus clash and the codec times out (-110), so no card forms. Also: wcd937x_reset uses gpiod_set_value on a sleeping GPIO (should be _cansleep). The boot's kernel log is kept on the lab machine. Analysis of the WCD boot (log on the lab machine): at 11.92 s the SoundWire controller 62ed0000 reports a bus clash right after the codec's reset (11.90-11.91 s) - the WCD leaves reset while the controller drives the bus; at 15.64 s the DSP switches both LPASS clocks off (q6afe clk 780 and 781, freq 0) before the codec's SoundWire device has finished initialising, which times out at 17.39 s (-110) and fails the card. Likely the macro's runtime power management dropping its clocks a few seconds after probe. Next experiment: keep the macro clocks on through SoundWire initialisation (no autosuspend while the WCD enumerates); then the reset order. Minor: qcom,dmic-sample-rate and qcom,mbhc-buttons-vthreshold-microvolt missing from the device tree; wcd937x_reset should use gpiod_set_value_cansleep.
title: Microphone: check, and make it work

note: Plasma Mobile (fresh Nura image, sound fixes applied on the phone): speakers were silent with the whole chain playing. Two causes, both confirmed: (1) the image restores a saved mixer state with both amplifiers' digital volume at 0 = -110 dB; (2) a tas2562 driver bug: setting the Digital Volume Control changes only the driver's cache, the chips (page 2, 0x0c-0x0f) stay at -110 dB. Writing 0x40000000 straight into both chips with i2cset made sound work: the user heard YouTube in Firefox, 2026-11-10. Not persistent: after a power-off the restore and the driver bug bring the silence back. Needed: the driver fix (upstream-tas2562-volume), and until then a boot-time step that writes the volume into the chips. Root cause found and fixed 2026-11-10: the tas2562 driver's maximum volume (0 dB) read past the end of its lookup table, which muted the amps; with two more faults (the latch byte written first, resume skipping bytes). Fixed module installed and proven on the phone by I2C reads; every flash bakes it in. Listen on Plasma when it is next run.
title: Plasma Mobile: speakers silent, the chain playing

Plan: one CLI in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools reading the device manifest (device.toml): phone (find over USB or Wi-Fi, run commands with no quoting layer), kernel install/try/log/remove (the safe test-kernel boot proven on surya 2026-11-10: one try by boot counting, a stalled initramfs saves its log and reboots into stock), provision, test (the checks, results as versioned JSON lines), tone. note: The sensors firmware on SM7150 (surya) rebuilds its registry from the configs at start and writes temp.json beside it; hexagonrpcd refuses every write by design, and does not serve registry/../sns_reg_version either. Sensors need both: the version marker served (patch drafted against hexagonrpc v0.5.0-20) and writes to a per-device writable copy of the registry (as Android persist is writable). An upstream change to linux-msm/hexagonrpc; until then the sensors service stays off on surya.
title: ADSP sensors: let hexagonrpcd serve a writable sensor registry

note: The boot hang (RCU stalls) with the WCD937x patch is the aoncc clock controller at 0x03380000, an SM8250 address with nothing near it in the SM7150 tree: with only aoncc disabled the phone boots (2026-11-09). Without aoncc the VA macro has no mclk, so the macros, SoundWire and the sound card stay deferred. Fix as SM8250 does: no aoncc, VA macro mclk from q6afecc. Audit tools and results in linux-phone-oco/surya-lab and on linux-phone-oco/linux#1.
